title: Add invocation mini-snapshots and entropy-based alert coalescer to reduce noise and egress
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: In high-volume multimodal workloads we observed a large fraction of paging alerts and noisy oncall churn caused by many low-information invocation traces (repetitive prompts or identical short completions). This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) invocation mini-snapshots — compact, structured snapshots captured at decision points that store a small, privacy-safe summary of the invocation for debugging and SLO analysis; and 2) an entropy-based alert coalescer — a service-level component that groups alerts based on token-entropy signatures so that low-information storms are coalesced before paging. Goals: reduce egress/logging costs, keep enough context for triage, and reduce alert fatigue while preserving signal for anomalous high-entropy invocations. What changed (high level): - New snapshotter component in the observability runtime that emits a compact JSON blob for sampled invocations. Each mini-snapshot includes: invocation id, model variant, route, timestamp, prompt fingerprint, first/last N token hashes (configurable), an anonymized token-length histogram, latency phases (queue/serve/stream), and cost estimate. All fields are structured and small by design (defaults under ~1 KB). Sensitive material is hashed or summarized; no PII/raw prompt text is persisted by default. - Entropy coalescer service: consumes mini-snapshots and span metadata, computes a lightweight token-entropy signature per invocation and groups invocations that fall below an entropy threshold into aggregated alerts. Configurable policy supports: immediate coalesce, buffered window (default 30s), or per-route overrides for strict routes. - Dashboard and alerting changes: added an aggregated "Invocation Snapshot" dashboard with a sparkline of coalesced-alert volume, entropy distribution heatmap, and per-route retention usage panel. Updated the alert runbooks with guidance on interpreting coalesced alerts. - CLI/Config: runtime config flags to control sampling rate, token hash window size, snapshot retention TTL, and entropy thresholds. - Tests & perf: microbenchmarks for snapshot serialization/deserialization and end-to-end integration smoke tests for coalescing logic. The tests include a synthetic workload that demonstrates a ~42% reduction in duplicate pages in our replaybench. Backwards compatibility: The snapshotter is opt-in via a new feature flag (obs.mini_snapshots.enabled=false by default). Entropy coalescer is deployed behind the obs-alerting feature flag and defaults to monitoring only non-critical routes. Migration notes: Customers who enable mini-snapshots will see a small additional metric (obs.snapshot_count) and may opt into longer retention for support. Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary clusters first, then gradual expansion over two weeks. See release_notes below for next steps.

review_thread: Ethan: Can we guarantee that mini-snapshots contain no raw prompt text? Priya: Yes — snapshots only include hashed prompt fingerprints and token hashes; we added a unit test to assert the scrubber drops raw prompt fields. Linnea: The entropy computation seems expensive at scale; have you budgeted CPU/ram? Priya: Entropy code is constant-time with a bounded window and runs in the coalescer service (separate process) — added microbenchmarks showing ~0.8 us per-invocation for a 32-token window. Marco: Need a graceful degradation path if the coalescer falls behind. Priya: Added a fallback policy that disables coalescing and forwards raw alerts to pager after a configurable backlog threshold. After addressing comments we re-ran CI and Ethan granted approval. Linnea approved after we reduced default sampling to 0.1% for high-throughput routes. Marco requested the runbook link which was added. Final: 3 approvals, ready to merge.

release_notes:
- Introduce opt-in invocation mini-snapshots (compact structured telemetry) for improved triage and lower egress.
- Add entropy-based alert coalescer to reduce paging from low-information invocation storms.
- New dashboard: Invocation Snapshots and entropy distribution.
- Config flags: obs.mini_snapshots.enabled, obs.snapshot_sampling_rate, obs.snapshot_window_tokens, obs.entropy_coalesce_threshold.
Note: Feature is opt-in; enable via runtime flags or Console feature toggle.
